findings.title: Synchronous main-thread signal bridge can re-enter CliJob's non-reentrant lock
findings.precise_counterexample: CliJob.run holds self._lock on the same main thread while checking cancellation and constructing Popen. If SIGINT or SIGTERM arrives in that region, Python invokes the enclosure handler on that main thread; handler calls job.cancel, which tries to acquire the already-held non-reentrant threading.Lock. The interrupted code cannot resume to release it. The same re-entrant path exists for a signal during main-thread check_live or cancel. This can deadlock the coordinator supervisor, leave the shared lane held, and prevent cooperative cancellation from reaching the actual child.
findings.required_resolution: Keep the enclosure signal bridge from synchronously acquiring CliJob locks in a main-thread signal handler. Reuse the product's deferred/cooperative cancellation contract without forced coordinator termination; no new worker-ownership framework is required. Preserve the existing late live-cancel checks and lane lifetime.
findings.review_note: The earlier advice to bridge signals through job.cancel omitted this main-thread lock re-entry condition; this review corrects that omission.
findings.execution_status: Source-derived path only; no hanging control, test or Native process executed.

resolved_v1_findings.title: Forced coordinator termination could interrupt inner worker cleanup
resolved_v1_findings.readback: The new enclosure calls existing CliJob.run, whose watchdog sends SIGINT and waits; it does not force-kill the coordinator or manufacture cleanup_complete. The shared lane encloses job execution, retained evidence readback and final publication. The scope explicitly disclaims permanent descendant certification, aggregate RSS observation and a hard whole-time quota.
resolved_v1_findings.status: cooperative-contract source correction present, subject to the signal bridge finding

resolved_v1_findings.title: Cold preparation was excluded from the original whole-slice budget
resolved_v1_findings.readback: Both outer and child subtract recorded preparation wall/full-CPU costs plus the explicit conservative 2-second preparation-publication budget charge from their reserves. Both add the charged preparation costs to recorded totals. The protocol labels the charge as a budget charge rather than measured runtime and retains the complete outer 180-second acceptance scope.

fresh calls job.check_live before and after a positive material readback. A post-f.publish live-cancel exception is passed through existing f.publish with a failing stable callback, archiving a canonical positive and correcting passed/status through account.
Outer account clears passed on cancellation or any noncompleted status; child account retains the same noncompleted-status clearing and terminal-status exit check.
No outer cleanup_complete or whole-tree RSS claim is introduced. Existing inner worker time/log/RSS/disk/network guards remain, and completed material inventories retain the existing bounded reader.
Flat owned board name and exact actual route source/hash correspondence remain required. Version/context/whole-board scope and software-intent versus human/application distinctions are unchanged.
